university_description_1: Inspired by the approximately four-thousand-year-old heritage of the Barind region and the ancient centers of learning such as Nalanda, Taxila, Somapura Mahavihara, Mahasthangarh, and Mainamati, we are preparing to launch the experimental activities of the "VisvaBangla Spiritual University."
university_description_2: This initiative is the result of more than fifteen years of research aimed at establishing a university based on universal humanitarian meditation, knowledge, education, and spiritual guidance for self-development and self-purification — especially for non-communal Sufi-oriented spiritual seekers.
university_description_3: Already, approximately <highlight>{{count}} participants</highlight> from Rajshahi and surrounding regions — including Sufi practitioners, spiritual seekers, laborers, and ordinary non-communal people — have been attending weekly thematic humanitarian philosophy classes, free meditation sessions, and Sufi spiritual education programs regularly.
nature_description: This organization operates as a voluntary organization dedicated to improving human life and society. Its operational area initially covers the Rajshahi district, with the potential to expand to other districts and sub-districts with the approval of the registration authority.

foundation_story: After many years of research in education, art, and literature, <highlight>Dr. Shah Syed Hasib Ul Hasan Raza</highlight> established the social and cultural organization named <highlight>VisvaBangla Foundation</highlight> with the vision of creating institutions such as the World Human Religion Center, World Meditation Center, and VisvaBangla Spiritual University — based on a universal, non-communal, non-political, and deeply humanitarian philosophy of life focused on meditation, knowledge, education, spiritual guidance, research, and publications.
registration_description: The organization was officially registered under the Ministry of Social Welfare of the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh through the District Social Services Office, Rajshahi.

faq_description: Everything you need to know before joining us.
faq_question_1: Do I need prior experience to join a meditation class?
faq_answer_1: Not at all! Our programs are open to everyone — from complete beginners to experienced practitioners. Our teachers will guide you every step of the way.
faq_question_2: How do I join a free meditation session?
faq_answer_2: You can join by contacting us through this form, calling us directly, or visiting our center in Rajshahi. All sessions are completely free of charge.
faq_question_3: What should I bring to my first class?
faq_answer_3: Just bring comfortable clothing and an open mind. We provide all necessary materials. Water bottles are welcome.
faq_question_4: Is the VisvaBangla Spiritual University really free?
faq_answer_4: Yes, absolutely. All programs — meditation, spiritual education, and knowledge sessions — are entirely free of cost, open to every seeker regardless of background.
faq_question_5: Can I volunteer as a teacher or researcher?
faq_answer_5: Yes! Any knowledgeable scholar or researcher may voluntarily teach in our classes. Please contact us to discuss how you can contribute.

spiritual_university_subtitle: Universal Humanitarian Philosophy Institute of Meditation, Knowledge, Education and Spiritual Guidance
spiritual_university_description_1: Inspired by the approximately four-thousand-year-old heritage of the Barind region and the ancient centers of learning such as <highlight>Nalanda, Taxila, Somapura Mahavihara, Mahasthangarh, and Mainamati</highlight>, we are preparing to launch the experimental activities of the VisvaBangla Spiritual University under the initiative of VisvaBangla Foundation.
spiritual_university_description_2: This initiative is the outcome of more than <highlight>fifteen years of research</highlight> aimed at establishing a university based on universal humanitarian meditation, knowledge, education, and spiritual guidance for self-development and self-purification — especially for non-communal Sufi-oriented spiritual seekers.
pillar_meditation_desc: Structured meditation programs rooted in universal humanitarian philosophy for self-purification and inner liberation.
pillar_knowledge_desc: Research-based spiritual and philosophical knowledge simplified and freely distributed to all seekers.
pillar_education_desc: Free, open education for underprivileged working-class people deprived of formal learning opportunities.
pillar_spiritual_guidance_desc: Guidance from experienced Sufi practitioners, researchers, and respected spiritual teachers.
open_to_everyone_desc: Any interested individual may join this humanitarian educational philosophy at any time. Any knowledgeable scholar or researcher may voluntarily teach in these classes. Everything is conducted entirely free of charge.
features_description: Researchers and spiritual practitioners simplify modern scientific and research-based humanitarian and spiritual knowledge for educationally deprived ordinary people. Weekly and monthly classes include analytical and evidence-based discussions on different levels of spiritual consciousness.
core_principle_desc_1: This humanitarian institution will be dedicated to realizing a noble vision. Here,
core_principle_highlight: self-purification will be regarded as the foundation of all well-being
core_principle_desc_2: — the path toward a compassionate, just, and service-oriented human society.
cta_desc: Join our free weekly classes — open to all, no registration fee, no commitment.
vision_quote: "Nowhere in the world has a university been established solely for the purpose of freely distributing universal humanitarian and spiritual meditation-based knowledge dedicated to self-purification. We dream of building a peaceful, compassionate, non-communal, and humanitarian world through the study, research, and publication of the philosophies of the great human beings of the world."
vision_quote_footer: — Dr. S. M. Hasib Ul Hasan, Founder
vision_context: In today's capitalist and materialistic social system, essential aspects of human life such as education, healthcare, employment, and housing have become commodities. This institution stands as a counter-vision — a sanctuary of free knowledge, compassion, and spiritual liberation.
vision_participants_desc: People from Rajshahi and neighboring districts — including followers of Sufism, Gurubadi and Tariqa traditions, spiritual seekers, laborers, and ordinary non-communal people devoted to self-discovery — have participated in weekly thematic classes focused on humanitarian philosophy, meditation, spiritual knowledge, and Sufi teachings.
vision_teachers_desc: Teachers, researchers, and scholars from various educational institutions and universities are working with us to simplify and freely distribute research-based spiritual and philosophical knowledge among underprivileged working-class people — including laborers, day workers, porters, blacksmiths, potters, fishermen, and weavers.
